TEXAS TRIBUNE: Drifting anti-immigrant buoys briefly close 2 Rio Grande bridges

July 17, 2026 | 🟢

100+ federal border buoys broke loose in the flooded Rio Grande and drifted toward Eagle Pass — closing two international bridges (~9,000 vehicles/day) for hours.

CBP swore "Operation River Wall" — 500+ miles of buoy barriers — could survive a 100-year flood. It didn't survive one July storm. The barrier built to stop people ended up stopping legal cross-border trade.

• CBP said the system was "engineered to withstand a 100-year flood"
• ~9,000 vehicles cross the two shuttered bridges daily

REUTERS: The economic goal that never came — World Cup falls short of boosting Mexico

July 17, 2026 | 🟡

Reuters: the World Cup added about $2B to Mexico — 0.1% of GDP, and less than half the $5.6B Mexico received in remittances in May alone.

The same piece names the real drag: not the tournament, but USMCA uncertainty and weak investment — i.e. Trump's trade threats, not Mexico's hosting.

• "The World Cup will not structurally change the trajectory of the Mexican economy" — Rankia chief economist
• Banamex: total impact ~$2 billion, about 0.1% of GDP

USA TODAY: Mexico's president accepting Trump's invitation to attend World Cup final

July 18, 2026 | 🟢

Sheinbaum says she got a "direct invitation" from Trump to Sunday's final at MetLife — her first face-to-face with him since December's draw. US outlets frame it as a diplomatic reset.

After a month of DEA "cartel" accusations and disputes over Mexicans killed in ICE custody, the two share a VIP box. Cooperation and confrontation running on parallel tracks.

• Sheinbaum: received a "direct invitation" from Trump
• Bloomberg: the final draws the three leaders "for first meeting since December"

🇲🇽🌎 THIRD ROUND OF T-MEC TALKS LANDS IN MEXICO CITY

US trade rep Jamieson Greer travels to Mexico City July 22–24 for the third bilateral round of T-MEC review — steel, aluminum, autos, agriculture, labor and electronic payments, with Marcelo Ebrard across the table. After July's mandatory joint review Washington declined to extend the pact to 2042, so it now runs on annual revisions through 2036, per El Financiero.

🔥🇲🇽 MEXICO'S BILLIONAIRE CLUB HIRED AN EX-CIA OFFICER TO LOBBY WASHINGTON

The Consejo Mexicano de Negocios — Mexico's billionaire club — paid $120,000 in 2025 to a lobbying firm staffed by retired CIA operations officer Enrique "Rick" de la Torre to work the US Treasury, State Department and USTR on T-MEC, Contralínea reports. De la Torre was "special guest" at a June dinner the investigation describes as Mexico's right and Washington sitting down to "chart a path of interventionism in the country."

🚨🇲🇽 QUINTANA ROO CUTS MURDERS 85% — TULUM HITS ZERO

Intentional homicides in Quintana Roo are down 85% since September 2024 — from a daily average of 2 killings to 0.3, the lowest June since 2015. Tulum has now gone two consecutive months without a single homicide. Sheinbaum presented the figures alongside security chief García Harfuch.

🇲🇽🏭 MEXICO PUTS AN AMMONIA MEGAPROJECT TO THE PEOPLE WHO LIVE THERE

The federal government opened five days of consultation tables with Mayo-Yoreme communities over the GPO ammonia plant on Ohuira bay, Topolobampo — environmental monitoring, regional benefits, the bay's condition, permits. The stated goal: decisions "based on technical evidence" and "respect for indigenous peoples' rights." A megaproject run past the people who live beside it, not around them.

🇲🇽🌎 MEXICO SNUBS RUBIO'S "LEFT-WING TERRORISM" SUMMIT

61 governments attended Marco Rubio's Washington summit against "left-wing extremist terrorism." Mexico, Brazil and Singapore stayed home. Sheinbaum said the event was "more political than an issue really tied to combating criminal groups," so Mexico informed the State Department it wouldn't attend.

🇲🇽🏭 WALL STREET BETS ON MEXICO — BLACKROCK SEES INVESTMENT GRADE HOLDING

El Financiero reports the world's largest asset manager expects Mexico to keep its investment grade. "We're confident we'll maintain investment grade," said José Luis Ortega, BlackRock México's head of active fixed income, pointing to skilled labor, geography, and North American integration. It tracks a wider shift: Wall Street now favors Mexican assets over Brazil's, even with T-MEC talks unresolved. The "failing state" narrative doesn't survive contact with the people actually moving the money.

🇲🇽🚆 IZTAPALAPA GETS 1.8 BILLION PESOS AGAINST THE FLOODS

Clara Brugada is putting 1.8 billion pesos into flood defense for Iztapalapa — nine underground storm tanks beneath Calzada Zaragoza, 54 deep-drainage projects, and a kilometer-long collector rerouting wastewater to regulation basins. "The full right to water and security," she said, calling it a repair of historic inequality in the city's northeast. Public works for exactly the neighborhoods the neoliberal decades left to flood.
